title.en: Noir single hard key with a controlled black level

summary: Light from one hard source at a steep ratio and let most of the frame fall away, while holding the black level just above zero.
objective: A single shadow set is present at a key-to-fill ratio of at least 8:1, and the darkest sampled pixel is still above zero.
intent_signals: make it look like film noir
high contrast black and white mood
the scene is too evenly lit
example_prompts: Light a single figure so the shadow falls across the wall behind them.
Set an interrogation-room mood with one source and no fill.
Give an alley scene a hard raking light and deep shadow.
not_for: Scenes that must show every surface clearly, where losing half the frame is a fault.
Product or measurement work that needs even, shadow-free coverage.

principles: One source means one shadow set. The moment a second light casts, the look collapses into ordinary dramatic lighting.
The ratio is the style. Below about 8:1 the image reads as moody; at 8:1 and above it reads as noir.
Black level is a decision, not an accident. Shadow cores held at a few percent above zero keep shape information and stop the image looking like a rendering error.
Hard light comes from a small source. Narrow the cone and reduce the penumbra rather than raising the intensity.
What is hidden carries the composition. Choose which third of the subject is lit before choosing where the light goes.
implementation: Use one SpotLight at about 900 cd with decay 2, a 28 deg cone and penumbra 0.15, positioned high and to one side (62 deg elevation, 300 deg azimuth).
Allow only a HemisphereLight at 0.1 as fill; anything more collapses the ratio, and no rim light is used.
Keep a dark gradient background rather than flat black so the frame still has a horizon and the subject silhouette has something to sit against.
Use AgX tone mapping at exposure 0.85: its shadow handling keeps the cores separable at this ratio where a steeper curve would crush them.
Add grain at 0.08, higher than any other profile here, because a nearly black frame shows banding first and grain hides it.
Check the black level by sampling the darkest region; if it reads zero, raise the hemisphere fill by 0.02 at a time rather than raising exposure.
observable_checks: Exactly one shadow set is visible in frame; every shadow traces back to the same source.
A sampled neutral card in the key reads at least eight times the value of the same card in the fill.
The darkest pixel in frame is above zero, confirming the black level rule.
A grayscale screenshot still reads as a composition, since colour is contributing almost nothing here.

creative_affordances: The key colour can be any temperature, including hard cyan or sodium orange, as long as it stays the only caster.
Practical sources like a sign or a window can be added as visible emissive elements provided they do not become a second key.
known_limits: Every number in this profile was tuned for AgX tone mapping at exposure 0.85; under a different tone-mapping curve or exposure the intensities and fog density must be re-derived, not copied.
The 8:1 ratio was tuned against AgX at exposure 0.85; under ACESFilmic the same lights read a stop flatter and the ratio must be re-derived.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.

defaults.rationale: A noir read comes from one hard source and a ratio steep enough that most of the frame is unlit, so a single narrow spot at 900 cd works against a hemisphere fill of just 0.1 for a ratio well past 8:1. AgX at 0.85 is chosen over a steeper curve because it keeps the shadow cores separable instead of crushing them, which is what makes the black-level rule achievable; the dark gradient sky and 0.08 grain exist to stop the near-black areas banding or reading as an empty buffer. Kelvin-to-hex conversions here are authored approximations, not colorimetric transforms (2700K~#ffb46b, 3200K~#ffc58f, 4500K~#ffe4c4, 5600K~#fff4e5, 6500K~#ffffff, open shade 8000K~#cfe0ff).

values.time_of_day: night interior or unlit alley; no ambient daylight

rim.note: deliberately absent; a rim would give a second read and soften the ratio

lights.ratio: key:fill >= 8:1 measured on a neutral card; 12:1 is still within the style

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

post.black_level: darkest sampled pixel held at 3-6% linear, never clipped to zero

never: a fill light strong enough to bring the ratio under 8:1
shadow cores clipped to pure black
a flat black background with no gradient
